dataflow.outcome: persistent prepared CAS content/name mismatch for one raced file
dataflow.source: mutable selected-scope file after initial raw-hash verification
dataflow.summary: selected-scope pathname -> CLI first read/hash -> prepare-stage reopen/hash -> prepared CAS publication

impact.why: The trusted prepared CAS namespace can contain an object whose content does not match its name, causing bounded provenance/search/evidence integrity loss.

likelihood.why: The path is real, but the exploit depends on a post-check race and no deterministic barrier was identified.

limitations: No confidentiality, outside-scope write, or code execution impact was demonstrated.

reachability.attacker: lower-trust local or synced-folder contributor to the selected root
reachability.entrypoint: ordinary `kcs index` processing of the mutable file
reachability.outcome: prepared object name and body disagree inside one scope-local store
reachability.summary: Local CLI indexing only; exploitation requires concurrent selected-root write/rename authority and favorable scheduling between the CLI hash check and prepare reopen.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust selected-root contributor lets version A pass the first read, replaces the pathname with version B before prepare, and causes KCS to publish A bytes at a prepared object path named for B.

codeEvidence.explanation: The CLI hashes the bytes it just read and rejects stale scan-state mismatches, but then forwards `input_path` rather than the verified byte buffer to `prepare_units()`.
codeEvidence.label: CLI verifies only the first read

codeEvidence.explanation: `PrepareStageRequest` carries both `raw_hash` and `input_path`, creating an expected binding point between the caller-verified identity and the bytes prepare consumes.
codeEvidence.label: Prepare reopens the pathname and hashes later bytes

codeEvidence.explanation: `prepare_units()` reads `request.input_path` again and computes `prepared_hash` from that second byte buffer without comparing it to `request.raw_hash`.
codeEvidence.label: Prepare derives prepared hashes from the reopened bytes

codeEvidence.explanation: The caller combines `prepare.prepared_object_hashes` from the second read with `bytes` from the first read, setting up a content/name mismatch when the pathname changes between reads.
codeEvidence.label: Caller writes the first-read bytes under prepare-returned hashes

codeEvidence.explanation: `write_prepared_objects()` builds the object path from `prepared_hash` and, for the text-native single-unit case, publishes `bytes` from the caller. Atomic publication does not validate that the body hashes to the destination name.
codeEvidence.label: Prepared CAS path is selected by hash but body comes from caller bytes

codeEvidence.explanation: Before `atomic_write_cas_object()`, the implementation should verify that `hash_bytes(object_bytes)` equals `prepared_hash`, or should make divergence impossible by preparing from the already verified bytes.
codeEvidence.label: Expected invariant

regressionTests: Force prepare to observe bytes different from the caller-verified buffer and require rejection.
Verify text prepared object content hashes to its object name before publication.
Verify PDF per-page prepared hashes are checked against the exact page bytes written.
remediation.summary: Prepare from the caller-verified bytes or a stable descriptor, and add a final `hash_bytes(object_bytes) == prepared_hash` assertion before publication.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that a prepared object name must be derived from the same bytes published at that name. The CLI validates the first read, `prepare_units()` reopens and hashes the path again without consuming or comparing `raw_hash`, and `write_prepared_objects()` publishes the first-read buffer under the second-read prepared hashes.

summary: The CLI verifies one byte buffer, passes only the mutable pathname to `prepare_units()`, and later writes the first-read bytes under prepared hashes derived from a second path read. A selected-root replacement between the two reads can publish a prepared CAS object whose name and contents disagree.
title: Prepare-stage reopen can poison prepared CAS identity

assertions: `PrepareStageRequest.raw_hash` is not consumed by `prepare_units()` as a byte-binding check.
`write_prepared_objects()` derives the destination from `prepared_hash` but can publish the caller-retained first-read bytes.
Atomic publication protects crash consistency, not content/name agreement.
limitations: No barrier-controlled replacement was run inside a live KCS store.
Race reliability and downstream consumer behavior beyond prepared CAS integrity were not measured.
validation.method: V10 exact static trace plus local synthetic regression probe
validation.summary: Source review confirms the two independent reads and the missing prepared-hash/object-byte equality check. The bundled PoC models the exact invariant violation with synthetic bytes and demonstrates that A can be written at B's prepared object name.
